Text: Arrays in Java have a {{c1::fixed::fixed or dynamic}} size after creation.
Extra: Once instantiated, you cannot expand or shrink a Java array.

Text: To find the size of an array, use the public field {{c1::length}}, whereas for a String, use the method {{c2::length()}}.
Extra: Notice that `length` for arrays is a field (no parentheses), while `length()` for String is a method call.

Text: In Java, a multidimensional array is actually an {{c1::array of arrays}}.
Extra: This allows nested arrays to have different lengths (ragged arrays).

Text: A runtime exception thrown when accessing index 5 on an array of length 5 is {{c1::ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException}}.
Extra: Indices range from 0 to 4.

Text: To copy a portion of an array natively and efficiently, use the {{c1::System.arraycopy()}} method.
Extra: This is a native method that operates directly on memory.

Text: Under the hood, `Arrays.sort()` uses the {{c1::Dual-Pivot Quicksort}} algorithm for primitive arrays.
Extra: This algorithm provides average O(N log N) performance but is unstable.

Text: For object arrays, `Arrays.sort()` uses the stable {{c1::Timsort}} algorithm.
Extra: Timsort is a hybrid of Merge Sort and Insertion Sort.

Text: Calling the `clone()` method on a multidimensional array performs a {{c1::shallow}} copy of the references.
Extra: The row references are copied, but they still point to the same sub-arrays.

Text: To print a multidimensional array as a readable String, you must use {{c1::Arrays.deepToString()}}.
Extra: `Arrays.toString()` on a 2D array will only print class name hashcode representations for the inner arrays.

Text: The default value for primitive `boolean` array elements is {{c1::false}}.
Extra: Numeric elements initialize to 0 or 0.0.

Text: To print a one-dimensional array cleanly as a String, use the method {{c1::Arrays.toString()}}.
Extra: Prints elements separated by commas inside square brackets.

Text: The default value initialized for all reference type elements in a newly allocated object array is {{c1::null}}.
Extra: You must instantiate each object index separately before usage.

Text: If `binarySearch()` cannot find a key, it returns a negative value calculated as {{c1::-(insertionPoint) - 1}}.
Extra: This encodes where the element should be placed to preserve order.

Text: Declaring an anonymous array on the fly (e.g. passing to a method) requires the {{c1::new int[]}} syntax.
Extra: For example: `print(new int[]{1, 2});`.

Text: Arrays are objects stored in the {{c1::Heap}} memory, and their references are stored in the {{c2::Stack}} memory.
Extra: This is standard behavior for all reference types in Java.
